spans.s:
√daṃś or daś (dáśati [746]; dadáṃśa;
daśiṣyáti; daṣṭá; daṃṣṭvā́; -dáśya).
bite. [cf. δάκνω, ‘bite’; Goth. tahjan,
‘rend, tear.’]

dáṃṣṭra, m. large tooth; tusk; fang.
[√daṃś, 1185b.]

daṃṣṭrin, a. having tusks or large teeth.
[daṃṣṭra.]

dánt [396], m. tooth. [cf. ὀδόντα, Lat.
dentem, Goth. tunϸus, AS. tōð, Eng. tooth,
Old High Ger. zand, Ger. Zahn, ‘tooth.’]

dānta, a. tamed, mild; subdued (as to
one's passions); as subst. Dānta, name of
a son of Bhīma. [ppl. of √dam, 955a.]

dā́na, n. giving, imparting; gift. [√1dā,
1150: cf. Lat. dōnum, ‘gift.’]

dāna-dharma, m. the virtuous practice
of alms-giving.
1dā́nu, f. Dānu, name of a demon, 70^18.
